snapshot.name: Location Input Feature
snapshot.description: Implement a location input interface in React Native that allows users to enter and manage two distinct location points: their current location and a destination. This feature should provide a user-friendly way to capture geographic information, likely for navigation or location-based services. The implementation should leverage React Native components for cross-platform mobile compatibility, integrate with the existing Jest testing framework for unit and integration tests, and follow the project's Babel transpilation setup. Consider whether location data should be automatically detected, manually entered, or both, and ensure the component handles location validation and state management appropriately.

stories.title: Phase 1: Location Data Model and Persistence Layer
stories.description: Establish Flow-typed data structures for location points, create a local persistence service for recent locations, and set up the foundation for location state management. This phase defines the core data models and storage mechanism that all subsequent features depend on.
stories.objective: Define Location and RecentLocation data structures with Flow types and implement AsyncStorage persistence
acceptance_criteria: Location and RecentLocation Flow types defined with all required fields including validated flag
LocationStorage service persists locations to AsyncStorage with max 20 recent items
Duplicate locations increment frequency counter instead of creating duplicates
Jest tests cover save, retrieve, delete, and frequency increment scenarios
Platform-specific test files exist for iOS and Android with identical test logic
implementation_notes: Create src/types/Location.js with Flow type definitions: type Location = { latitude: number, longitude: number, address: string, timestamp: number, validated: boolean }
Define type RecentLocation = { ...Location, id: string, frequency: number } for tracking frequently used locations
Create src/services/LocationStorage.js with AsyncStorage-based persistence using React Native's AsyncStorage API
Implement getRecentLocations(): Promise<RecentLocation[]> to retrieve last 20 locations sorted by frequency and recency
Implement saveLocation(location: Location): Promise<void> that adds to recent locations, increments frequency if duplicate address, maintains max 20 items
Implement deleteRecentLocation(id: string): Promise<void> for user-initiated removal
Follow callback-based async pattern from GooglePlacesAutocomplete: use .then() chains rather than async/await
Add Flow comment header (@flow) to all new files following project conventions
Create comprehensive Jest tests in __tests__/LocationStorage.test.js with platform-specific variants (__tests__/LocationStorage.ios.test.js, __tests__/LocationStorage.android.test.js)
Test scenarios: save new location, increment frequency on duplicate, maintain 20-item limit, retrieve sorted results, delete location

stories.title: Phase 2: Location Input Component with GPS and Google Maps Integration
stories.description: Build the LocationInput React Native component that handles GPS auto-detection for current location and manual entry with Google Maps Places autocomplete for destination. Integrate with the persistence layer and implement offline-first validation strategy.
stories.objective: Create LocationInput component with GPS detection, Places autocomplete, and offline-capable location validation
acceptance_criteria: LocationInput component displays GPS detection button for current location with loading state
GooglePlacesAutocomplete integration provides destination suggestions with callback-based selection
Recent locations list displays and allows quick re-selection of previous destinations
Component gracefully handles offline scenarios by setting validated: false and allowing submission
Minimal validation errors display without blocking user submission
Jest tests cover GPS detection, autocomplete selection, recent locations, and offline scenarios
Platform-specific test files verify iOS and Android rendering
implementation_notes: Create src/services/GoogleMapsService.js to wrap Google Maps Geocoding and Places APIs with callback-based interface
Implement geocodeAddress(address: string, onSuccess: (Location) => void, onError: (error) => void): void using Google Maps Geocoding API
Implement getPlacePredictions(input: string, onSuccess: (predictions) => void, onError: (error) => void): void for autocomplete suggestions
Implement getPlaceDetails(placeId: string, onSuccess: (Location) => void, onError: (error) => void): void to get full location from place selection
Create src/services/LocationService.js as facade combining GPS detection, Google Maps, and offline handling
Implement getCurrentLocation(onSuccess: (Location) => void, onError: (error) => void): void using react-native-geolocation-service or built-in Geolocation API
Implement validateLocation(location: Location, onSuccess: (Location) => void, onError: (error) => void): void that attempts geocoding validation but allows submission with validated: false if offline
Create src/components/LocationInput.js as main React Native component with two sections: CurrentLocation (GPS button + display) and DestinationLocation (autocomplete input + recent locations list)

Component state: { currentLocation: ?Location, destination: ?Location, recentLocations: RecentLocation[], isLoadingCurrent: boolean, isLoadingDest: boolean, validationErrors: { [key: string]: string } }

CurrentLocation section: Button labeled 'Detect Current Location' that calls LocationService.getCurrentLocation(), shows loading spinner during detection, displays address or coordinates, shows minimal error message on failure

DestinationLocation section: GooglePlacesAutocomplete input (following existing pattern from codebase) with onPress callback handling place selection, displays recent locations below input for quick selection
Implement onLocationSelect(location: Location, type: 'current' | 'destination'): void that updates state, calls LocationStorage.saveLocation(), sets validated: false if offline
Add minimal validation: check latitude/longitude are valid numbers, address is non-empty string; show graceful error messages without blocking submission
Implement offline detection using NetInfo or similar; when offline, set validated: false on locations but allow submission
Add Flow type annotations to all functions and component props

Create Jest tests with snapshot testing for component rendering, mock GoogleMapsService and LocationService callbacks, test GPS detection flow, test autocomplete selection, test recent locations display
Create platform-specific test files following pattern: __tests__/LocationInput.ios.js and __tests__/LocationInput.android.js with platform-specific assertions

stories.title: Phase 3: Location Validation Service and Integration Testing
stories.description: Implement background validation service that validates unvalidated locations when connectivity returns, integrate LocationInput into the main App component, and add comprehensive integration tests. This phase ensures locations are validated asynchronously and the feature works end-to-end.
stories.objective: Create background validation service and integrate LocationInput with App, add integration tests
acceptance_criteria: LocationValidationService detects online/offline transitions and validates pending locations
Locations with validated: false are updated to validated: true after successful geocoding
Validation failures are handled gracefully without blocking app or throwing exceptions
LocationInput component is integrated into App.js and renders correctly
Integration tests verify complete offline-to-online validation flow
All tests pass on both iOS and Android platforms
Recent locations persist across app sessions and are available for quick re-selection
implementation_notes: Create src/services/LocationValidationService.js that monitors connectivity and validates pending locations
Implement startValidationService(): void that sets up NetInfo listener to detect online/offline transitions

Implement validatePendingLocations(): void that retrieves all locations with validated: false from LocationStorage, attempts geocoding validation via GoogleMapsService, updates validated: true on success, logs minimal errors on failure
Use callback-based pattern: validatePendingLocations calls LocationStorage.getRecentLocations().then(locations => { /* filter validated: false */ }).then(/* validate each */)
Implement stopValidationService(): void to clean up NetInfo listener
Add Flow types for validation state and service lifecycle

Modify App.js to initialize LocationValidationService on app startup: useEffect(() => { LocationValidationService.startValidationService(); return () => LocationValidationService.stopValidationService(); }, [])
Import and render LocationInput component in App.js with proper prop passing for location state updates

Create src/__tests__/LocationValidationService.test.js with Jest tests for: validation service initialization, pending location detection, successful validation callback, graceful error handling on validation failure

Create src/__tests__/integration/LocationInputIntegration.test.js with end-to-end scenarios: user enters location offline, app comes online, validation service validates location, location marked as validated
Mock NetInfo in tests to simulate online/offline transitions
Test scenario: save location with validated: false, trigger online event, verify LocationStorage updated with validated: true
Add snapshot tests for LocationInput component in different states: loading, with current location, with destination, with recent locations
Verify error handling is minimal: validation failures log to console but don't throw exceptions or block app
